keyVerseText: But unto the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom. righteousness: Gr. rightness, or, straightness
rootMeaning: The word εὐθύτης (euthýtēs) derives from the root εὐθύς (euthýs), which primarily conveys the idea of straightness or immediacy. Literally, it means 'straight' or 'level,' and figuratively it extends to notions of truth and directness. This root sense of being straight or upright enriches the English gloss of 'righteousness' by emphasizing moral integrity as a kind of spiritual straightness or rightness, rather than merely ethical correctness.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Hebrews 1:8, where it is translated as 'righteousness.' Its singular occurrence and consistent translation highlight its specialized use to denote a quality of moral and divine rectitude. The word's use in the Septuagint further associates it with the Hebrew concepts of uprightness and integrity, underscoring its role as a descriptor of God's just and true character.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding εὐθύτης as 'righteousness' rooted in the idea of straightness invites believers to see God's righteousness not just as abstract justice but as a perfectly aligned moral uprightness. This aligns with the biblical portrayal of God as the ultimate standard of truth and rectitude. For the Christian faith, this word underscores the nature of Christ's kingdom as founded on unchanging, straight truth, contrasting with human crookedness. It calls believers to pursue a life reflecting this divine straightness, which is only fully realized through Christ's redemptive work.
keyVerseReflection: Hebrews 1:8 declares, 'Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.' Here, εὐθύτης conveys that the authority and rule of the Son are characterized by perfect moral straightness and justice. The word enriches the verse by portraying God's reign as one governed by unwavering truth and integrity, assuring believers of the eternal and righteous nature of Christ's kingship.
